original_interpretation: Gartner's top-10 semiconductor vendor rankings include Apple, which does not sell chips to others, at US$20.5 billion in 2024 and US$24.6 billion in 2025; Gartner therefore values in-house (captive) chips of system companies as semiconductor revenue.
evidence_found: SRC-0235 Table 1 (Source: Gartner (January 2026)) row: "9 | Apple | $24,596M | 3.1% | $20,510M | 19.9%" (columns 2025 revenue, 2025 share, 2024 revenue, growth). SRC-0237 (Gartner April 2025 table) row "9 | Apple | 20,510 | 3.1 | 13.6".
correction: The dollar figures are verified. The second half ('Gartner therefore values in-house (captive) chips of system companies as semiconductor revenue') is our inference, not stated by Gartner; Gartner publishes no scope note. It is a reasonable reading because Apple does not sell chips to third parties, but the claim mixes an estimate with an interpretation.
notes: Numbers are tier-2 research_firm estimates; the inference should be a separate interpretation claim.

original_interpretation: Gartner raised its 2024 Nvidia semiconductor revenue estimate from about US$46 billion (preliminary, February 2025) to US$76.7 billion (final, April 2025), an upgrade of about US$30 billion.
evidence_found: "Nvidia's sales grew by 83.6 percent from about US$25 billion in 2023 to about US$46 billion in 2024." (preliminary) ... "Nvidia's sales grew by 120.1 percent from US$34.8 billion in 2023 to US$76.7 billion in 2024." ... "In Gartner's 'final' estimate of 2024 semiconductor revenue the analyst has raised Nvidia up by US$30 billion compared with the preliminary results." (eeNews Europe, 14 Apr 2025)
notes: Supported by industry_press (tier 2). claim_type 'fact' is acceptable for the fact of a revision as reported, but the underlying values are Gartner estimates.

original_interpretation: Gartner's preliminary 2023 estimate (January 2024) put Nvidia's semiconductor revenue at about US$24 billion, ranking it fifth.
evidence_found: "Nvidia does see Nvidia rising dramatically up the ranking with a annual semiconductor revenue growth of 56.4 percent. However, this represents total sales of just US$24 billion putting Nvidia fifth." (eeNews Europe, 16 Jan 2024)
notes: Note eeNews (SRC-0238, Apr 2025) describes the preliminary 2023 base in Gartner's Feb 2025 release as 'about US$25 billion', so Gartner's 2023 Nvidia figure moved 24 -> ~25 -> 34.8bn across vintages.

original_interpretation: Gartner's April 2025 vendor table restated Nvidia's 2023 semiconductor revenue at US$34.8 billion.
evidence_found: Gartner April 2025 table (as republished): header "2024 Rank | 2023 Rank | Vendor | 2024 Revenue | 2024 Market Share (%) | 2023 Revenue | 2024-2023 Growth (%)"; row "1 | 3 | NVIDIA | 76,692 | 11.7 | 34,846 | 120.1". Corroborated by eeNews: "from US$34.8 billion in 2023 to US$76.7 billion in 2024" (SRC-0238).
notes: SRC-0237 is an aggregator republication (tier 3), corroborated by SRC-0238 (industry_press).

original_interpretation: Gartner estimated Nvidia's 2025 semiconductor revenue at US$125.7 billion (15.8% share), the first vendor above US$100 billion.
evidence_found: Table 1 row: "1 | NVIDIA | $125,703M | 15.8% | $76,692M | 63.9%" (Source: Gartner (January 2026)); text: NVIDIA became "the first vendor to cross $100 billion semiconductor sales, contributing to over 35% of industry growth in 2025."
notes: Preliminary January 2026 estimate; Gartner may restate in its final vendor ranking (check CLM-0702 vintage).

original_interpretation: Gartner estimated that memory revenue grew 73.4% in 2024.
evidence_found: "The position shift among the top 10 semiconductor vendor revenue ranking is due to large demand for AI infrastructure buildout and an increase of 73.4% in memory revenue." (Gartner April 2025 release, republished by Design & Reuse)
notes: Aggregator republication of a Gartner release.

original_interpretation: IDC (September 2025) expected 2025 worldwide semiconductor revenue of US$800 billion, up 17.6% from US$680 billion in 2024.
evidence_found: "worldwide semiconductor revenue is expected to reach $800 billion in 2025, growing 17.6% year-over-year from $680 billion in 2024." (IDC press release, 8 Sep 2025)
notes: The 2025 figure is a forecast (Sept 2025); the metric records the 2024 base (US$680bn), which IDC states as actual. 800/680 = 1.176, consistent.

original_interpretation: IDC projected that in 2025 a single semiconductor company would for the first time surpass US$200 billion in annual revenue.
evidence_found: "For the first time, a single semiconductor company is projected to surpass $200 billion in annual revenue." (IDC press release, 8 Sep 2025)
notes: Projection, correctly typed as estimate.

original_interpretation: Omdia estimated that the semiconductor market surpassed US$830 billion in 2025, the second consecutive year of more than 20% growth.
evidence_found: "The semiconductor market surpassed $830 billion in 2025, marking the second consecutive year of more than 20% annual revenue growth." (MacTech republication of Omdia release, 24 Mar 2026)
notes: Lower bound correctly noted in metric methodology. Source is a news republication (tier 3) of an Omdia release.

original_interpretation: Omdia has tracked the semiconductor market since 2001.
evidence_found: "For the first time since Omdia began tracking the semiconductor market in 2001, the industry had two consecutive years with 20% annual revenue growth." (MacTech, 24 Mar 2026)
notes: Self-description, correctly typed reported_claim.

original_interpretation: Omdia estimated DRAM revenue rose from just over US$50 billion at the 2023 low to above US$150 billion in 2025.
evidence_found: "DRAM revenue has nearly tripled from just over $50 billion at the market low in 2023 to above $150 billion in 2025" (MacTech republication of Omdia, 24 Mar 2026)
notes: Lower bound (>150bn) noted in metric.

original_interpretation: Omdia estimated 3Q25 semiconductor industry revenue at US$216.3 billion, up 14.5% quarter-on-quarter, the first quarter above US$200 billion.
evidence_found: "the semiconductor market delivered a record-breaking performance in 3Q25 with industry revenue reaching $216.3 billion, up 14.5% quarter-over-quarter" ... "This marks the first time the global semiconductor market has exceeded $200 billion in a single quarter" (ICTbusiness, 14 Dec 2025, attributed to Omdia)
notes: Secondary news report (tier 3) of Omdia data.

original_interpretation: WSTS reported that the global semiconductor market reached US$702 billion in the first half of 2026, up 102% year on year, with memory up 305% and logic up 45%.
evidence_found: "The global semiconductor market reached 702 billion US dollars in the first half of 2026, representing a 102 percent increase year-over-year." ... "Memory, which expanded an exceptional 305 percent year-over-year. Logic also recorded outstanding growth of 45 percent." (WSTS Q2 2026 news release)

original_interpretation: After incorporating actual Q2 2026 data, WSTS's calculation for the full-year 2026 market rose to US$1,655 billion (about +108%) and for 2027 to about US$2.1 trillion (+29%), with memory now expected to grow 302%.
evidence_found: "The calculation for the full-year 2026 market reaches 1,655 billion US dollars, corresponding to annual growth of approximately 108 percent." ... "The calculation for 2027 reaches approximately 2.1 trillion US dollars, corresponding to annual growth of approximately 29 percent." ... "Memory, is now expected to grow by 302 percent (53 percentage points higher than the original estimate)." (WSTS Q2 2026 news release)
notes: A forecast-type calculation, correctly typed estimate.

original_interpretation: SIA reported 2025 sales growth by region of sale of 45.0% for Asia Pacific/All Other, 30.5% for the Americas, 17.3% for China and 6.3% for Europe, with Japan down 4.7%.
evidence_found: "Regionally, yearly sales were up in Asia Pacific/All Others (45.0%), the Americas (30.5%), China (17.3%), and Europe (6.3%), but were down in Japan (-4.7%)." (SIA, 6 Feb 2026)

original_interpretation: The roughly US$30bn upgrade to Nvidia explains essentially all of the US$29.9bn increase in Gartner's 2024 market total between its preliminary (US$626bn) and final (US$655.9bn) estimates.
evidence_found: Recomputed from sources re-opened in this run: Gartner Feb 2025 preliminary "Worldwide semiconductor revenue in 2024 totaled $626 billion, an increase of 18.1% from 2023" (SRC-0014, via gcom.pdo mirror of the same Gartner release; Nvidia row 45,988 US$M, 7.3%, +83.6%); Gartner April 2025 final "Worldwide semiconductor revenue totaled $655.9 billion in 2024, up 21% from $542.1 billion in 2023" with NVIDIA 76,692 US$M (SRC-0237); eeNews: "the analyst has raised Nvidia up by US$30 billion compared with the preliminary results" (SRC-0238). Total revision 655.9-626 = 29.9; Nvidia revision 76.692-45.988 = 30.7.
correction: Arithmetic holds (Nvidia +US$30.7bn vs total +US$29.9bn), but 'explains essentially all' is a causal reading Gartner does not state: other vendors' revisions net to about -US$0.8bn and could be larger offsetting moves. Better worded: 'The Nvidia upgrade (+US$30.7bn) is about the same size as the whole upgrade to the 2024 total (+US$29.9bn), so other vendors' revisions netted to roughly zero.' Also note the 2023 base was revised too (Gartner 533 -> 542.1).
notes: Inference; inputs CLM-0053, CLM-0054 re-checked against the releases in this run.

original_interpretation: Gartner's Nvidia figure is not Nvidia's reported total revenue, which covers chips plus systems, software and services over a fiscal year ending in late January; Gartner counts only the portion it treats as semiconductor revenue, by calendar year.
evidence_found: Nvidia 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SRC-0058): "Record full-year revenue of $130.5 billion, up 114%"; quarter ended "January 26, 2025"; Data Center "Full-year revenue rose 142% to a record $115.2 billion." Gartner (SRC-0237) NVIDIA 2024 revenue 76,692 US$M; Gartner (SRC-0235) 2025 125,703 US$M.
correction: Supported: Nvidia's fiscal year ends in late January (FY2025 ended 26 Jan 2025) and its reported FY2025 revenue (US$130.5bn) is far above Gartner's CY2024 figure (US$76.7bn), so Gartner is not using Nvidia's reported total. Not supported by any public source: that the gap is specifically the exclusion of 'systems, software and services' (Gartner publishes no reconciliation; part of the gap is the one-month fiscal offset and growth within the year). Keep as interpretation with that caveat.
notes: The researcher did not retrieve Nvidia's reported revenue; existing CLM-0145 (SRC-0058) gives it.

original_interpretation: Gartner's preliminary annual totals have been revised by -0.3% (2022), +1.7% (2023), +4.8% (2024) and +1.6% (2025) in later releases.
evidence_found: Inputs re-opened: 2022 601.7 (CLM-0700, verified) -> 599.6 (CLM-0701, verified); 2023 "Worldwide semiconductor revenue in 2023 totaled $533 billion, a decrease of 11.1% from 2022" (SRC-0109 via gcom.pdo mirror) -> "$542.1 billion in 2023" (SRC-0237); 2024 "$626 billion" (SRC-0014 via mirror) -> "$655.9 billion" (SRC-0237); 2025 "$793 billion" (SRC-0235) -> 805.3 (CLM-0702). Recomputed: -0.35%, +1.71%, +4.78%, +1.55%.
notes: Arithmetic correct. Caveat: the 2025 'later' value (US$805.3bn) comes from Gartner's April 2026 forecast release and is not labelled a final market-share figure (see CLM-0702, partially_verified), so the 2025 revision may not be final.

original_interpretation: Gartner's annual totals exceed WSTS's for the same year by about 2.9-4.4%: 2022 US$599.6bn vs US$574.1bn, 2023 US$542.1bn vs US$526.9bn, 2024 US$655.9bn vs US$630.5bn, 2025 US$805.3bn vs US$795.6bn (1.2%).
evidence_found: Recomputed: Gartner 599.6 / WSTS 574.084 = 1.0444; 542.1 / 526.885 = 1.0289; 655.9 / 630.549 = 1.0402; 805.3 / 795.640 = 1.0121. WSTS values confirmed in WSTS Blue Book XLSX (SRC-0223) 'Total Year' Worldwide rows: 574,084,194; 526,885,425; 630,548,606; 795,640,305 (thousand US$). Gartner 655.9/542.1 confirmed in SRC-0237.
notes: The claim's headline range '2.9-4.4%' covers 2022-2024 only; 2025 (1.2%) is stated separately, so the wording is consistent but should not be read as 'every year 2.9-4.4%'.

original_interpretation: The main identifiable reason Gartner's market is larger than WSTS's is population: Gartner counts captive chips of system companies (Apple alone US$20.5bn in 2024, about 80% of the US$25.4bn gap), which WSTS excludes as captive production; in 2025 Gartner's non-memory total exceeds WSTS's by about US$24bn while its memory total is about US$14bn lower.
correction: Arithmetic is right to rounding (2025 non-memory gap is US$23.4bn, stated as 'about US$24bn'). The causal statement ('main identifiable reason ... is population') is our interpretation: no publisher states it, and WSTS's population rule is only partially verified (CLM-0575; WSTS does value internal transfers to a member's own end-product divisions at market prices, CLM-0579, so captive output of reporting IDMs is in WSTS; what falls outside is chips of fabless system companies such as Apple bought from foundries). Apple's share of the gap is an illustration, not a decomposition.
notes: Interpretation built on CLM-0053, CLM-0036, CLM-0030, CLM-0702 and CLM-0575/CLM-0579.

original_interpretation: IDC's semiconductor population is wider than Gartner's or WSTS's: its 2024 base (US$680bn) is US$24bn above Gartner and US$49bn above WSTS, and its expectation of a company above US$200bn in 2025 is far above Gartner's US$125.7bn for the largest vendor, which suggests IDC counts company revenue beyond chips (e.g. Nvidia systems).
evidence_found: IDC (SRC-0241): "from $680 billion in 2024"; "For the first time, a single semiconductor company is projected to surpass $200 billion in annual revenue, reflecting the scale of AI focused datacenter driven growth."; IDC's service "includes foundry and automotive semiconductor coverage and revenue data collected from over 150 of the top semiconductor companies". Recomputed 680-655.9 = 24.1; 680-630.549 = 49.5.
correction: Arithmetic verified. The reason is unestablished: IDC says its data 'includes foundry' coverage, so part of the wider IDC total may be foundry revenue (which would double-count chip value) rather than Nvidia systems revenue. IDC does not name the >US$200bn company; the claim should list foundry inclusion as an equally plausible explanation.
notes: Nvidia's reported revenue (SRC-0058, FY2025 US$130.5bn) shows company-reported totals exceed Gartner's chip figure, consistent with the 'systems' reading but not proving it.

original_interpretation: Omdia estimated that Nvidia, Samsung, SK hynix and Micron together raised their share of semiconductor revenue from 24% in 2023 to 42% in 2025, and that top-ten company revenue grew 90% over 2023-2025 versus 8% for the rest of the market.
evidence_found: "revenue among the top ten semiconductor companies increased by 90% compared with 8% growth across the remainder of the market. Omdia says growth has been concentrated among memory suppliers and NVIDIA, highlighting how significantly AI demand is shaping the semiconductor market. Combined, these four companies increased their share of total semiconductor revenue from 24% in 2023 to 42% in 2025." (MacTech republication of Omdia, 24 Mar 2026, section 'Revenue consolidation among leading companies')
correction: The numbers are verified, but the source does not name Samsung, SK hynix and Micron; it says only 'memory suppliers and NVIDIA ... these four companies'. The three memory makers are our inference (they are the three large DRAM/HBM suppliers) and should be flagged as such in the claim and metric name.
notes: Also stated in source: total market grew about 53% between 2023 and 2025.

original_interpretation: For 2025 the publishers' totals span about US$795bn to over US$830bn: WSTS US$795.6bn, Gartner US$805.3bn and Omdia above US$830bn, a spread of at least 4% driven by differing populations rather than error.
evidence_found: Inputs: WSTS 2025 = 795,640,305 thousand US$ (SRC-0223); Gartner 805.3 (CLM-0702); Omdia "surpassed $830 billion in 2025" (SRC-0242). 830/795.64 = 1.043.
correction: The range and 'at least 4%' spread are correct. 'Driven by differing populations rather than error' is not established: none of the publishers discloses scope (CLM-0715, CLM-0726), and differences in estimation method (modelled vendor revenue vs member-reported billings, estimates for non-participants) are also possible. Say 'likely driven largely by differing populations and methods'.
notes: Consistent with existing CON-0015 (comparable=false).

original_interpretation: In June 2024 WSTS forecast the 2024 world semiconductor market at US$611 billion (+16.0%); the actual outcome was US$630.5 billion (+19.7%).
evidence_found: "WSTS has adjusted its Spring 2024 forecast upwards, projecting a 16.0 percent growth in the global semiconductor market compared to the previous year. The updated market valuation for 2024 is estimated at US$611 billion." (WSTS release, San Jose, June 4, 2024, p. 1). Outcome: Blue Book 2024 Worldwide 630,548,606 vs 2023 526,885,425 thousand US$ (SRC-0223) = +19.7%.

original_interpretation: In June 2024 WSTS forecast the 2025 world semiconductor market at US$687 billion (+12.5%), about 14% below the eventual US$795.6 billion.
evidence_found: "Looking ahead to 2025, WSTS forecasts a 12.5 percent growth in the global semiconductor market, reaching an estimated valuation of US$687 billion." (WSTS release, June 4, 2024, p. 1). Outcome 795,640,305 thousand US$ (SRC-0223); 687/795.64 - 1 = -13.7%.

original_interpretation: The July 2026 edition of the WSTS Blue Book data shows January-June 2026 billings of US$718.6 billion (Q1 US$304.9bn, Q2 US$413.7bn).
evidence_found: WSTS Historical Billings XLSX (July 2026 edition), sheet 1, 2026 block, row 'Worldwide': Q1 (O250) 304918931, Q2 (P250) 413729924 ("All numbers are in 1000 US$."). Sum = 718,648,855 thousand US$. Monthly Jan-Jun 82,925,862 + 103,671,953 + 118,321,116 + 115,800,518 + 140,466,438 + 157,462,968 = same total.
notes: Differs from WSTS's own Q2 2026 release (US$702bn, CLM-0731); already recorded as CON-0020. H1 2025 in the same file = 166,614,803 + 180,351,776 = 346.97bn, so Blue Book H1 growth is +107% vs +102% in the release.

original_interpretation: WSTS defines a regional 'market' as the region where a semiconductor maker sells the product to a third party (electronics makers, EMS companies or trading companies/distributors), regardless of the maker's nationality or where the chip was produced; chips sold in Japan count as the Japan market even if the buyer takes them abroad for assembly.
evidence_found: "WSTSの「半導体市場」は、半導体メーカーの国籍や生産工場の場所には関係なく、「半導体製品が半導体メーカーから第三者に販売された地域」を意味する。この「第三者」には、半導体ユーザーである電子機器メーカー、EMS、半導体を扱う商社などが含まれる。" ... "購入者が、購入した半導体製品を外国に運んで電子機器に組み入れたとしても、その半導体製品は日本市場に含まれる。" (WSTS Japan Council release, 3 Dec 2024, p. 1)
notes: Translation in the claim is faithful.

original_interpretation: The WSTS Japan Council stated in December 2024 that WSTS had 49 member semiconductor companies.
evidence_found: "なお、WSTSに加盟している半導体メーカーは現在49社である。" (WSTS Japan Council release, 3 Dec 2024, p. 1)
correction: WSTS's own website now states 50 member companies (CLM-0584, verified against SRC-0227). The 49 figure is correct as of December 2024 only.
notes: Accurate for its date; superseded by CLM-0584.

original_interpretation: WSTS forecast participants are prohibited from discussing future prices or supply-demand balance at forecast meetings because doing so would breach antitrust law; forecasts are built from members' own projections informed by WSTS statistics, macroeconomics and electronics trends.
evidence_found: "WSTSの市場予測は加盟会社がWSTS半導体市場統計を参照して作成した予測値を基に、マクロ経済や主要電子機器の動向も参考にしながら検討を加えて作成される。ただし将来の価格動向や需給バランス等に関しては、反トラスト法に抵触するため討議することを禁じられている。" (WSTS Japan Council release, 3 Dec 2024, p. 1)
notes: The link to forecast misses at memory-price turning points (in notes) is the researcher's inference, not the source's.

original_interpretation: All WSTS market forecasts are on a calendar-year basis, and the Autumn 2024 forecast was built on actual data through September 2024 at a meeting held 19-21 November 2024 in San Diego.
evidence_found: "今回の秋季市場予測は2024年9月までの実績値を基に作成した。なお、WSTSの半導体市場予測は全て暦年で行っている。"; "WSTS ... の2024年秋季半導体市場予測会議が11月19日～21日の3日間、米国のサンディエゴで開催された。" (WSTS Japan Council release, 3 Dec 2024, p. 1)
notes: Page 1 also states forecast meetings are held twice a year, in principle in May and November.

original_interpretation: The WSTS Japan Council put the 2023 Japanese semiconductor market at about ¥6.5637 trillion in yen terms, up 3.8%, even though the dollar-denominated Japan region fell in 2023.
evidence_found: "2023 年の日本の半導体市場は、前年比+3.8%、金額では約 6 兆 5,637 億円であった。" (p. 2); exchange rate "2023 年：140.4 円" (p. 2); 添付資料３ (p. 5): Japan 2022 48,158 / 2023 46,751 (M$), growth 2023 -2.9%; Japan(円ベース) 億円 2023 65,637, +3.8%.
notes: The dollar decline (-2.9%) is confirmed in the same release's p. 5 table, not only the Blue Book.
